newsitem.title: MEXICO: Seven dead in failed kidnap rescue bid in Mexico.
newsitem.headline: Seven dead in failed kidnap rescue bid in Mexico.

text.p: Six kidnappers and their hostage were killed in a failed rescue attempt by Mexican police in the northern state of Coahuila, police said on Friday.
A crack police rescue team stormed the kidnappers' hideout late on Thursday in the city of Torreon, some 450 miles (730 km) northwest of Mexico City, and shot dead all six abductors, police said.
But the hostage, an executive in a local agricultural company, was also killed in the exchange of gunfire between the police and the kidnappers.
"A firefight began between both sides and unfortunately the hostage was killed," a state police spokesman told Reuters in a telephone interview on Friday.
Local newspaper El Siglo reported that police first fired tear gas into the residence and then entered shooting their weapons after the abductors failed to come out.

The kidnappers, known locally as the Villalobos gang, abducted the executive, Jose Antonio Garcia Cantelli, earlier in the week and were demanding a two million peso ($250,000) ransom, the police spokesman said.
